title: Duplicate URL name makes the legacy fast route ambiguous
reasoning: Both legacy endpoints are registered with the same URL name, fast_on_date, while pointing to different route patterns and different views. Any code that reverses this name cannot express whether it wants /user/fasts/ or /fast/, so generated links can silently target the wrong legacy endpoint depending on Django's URL resolver behavior and declaration order. This is an API contract risk for the reviewed /api/user/fasts/ route because its named route is not unique.
recommendation: Give the two routes distinct names, for example fast_on_date and fast_on_date_without_user, and update any reverse() or frontend references accordingly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included fast tests exercise FastListView, FastByFeastDateView, and serializer day-number behavior, but they do not reverse or resolve the legacy fast_on_date route name.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a URL test that reverse('fast_on_date') resolves to the intended /api/user/fasts/ endpoint and that the /api/fast/ route has a separate name.
minimumFixScope: Change the duplicate name on one of the two legacy path declarations and adjust references that use the old ambiguous name.
